prompt.context: A ski manufacturer (snow-skis) has developed a revolutionary new ski technology. You, knowing very little about skis, have stumbled across them, and have seen a chance to become the Australian distributor for the product.
prompt.question: You are meeting the ski manufacturer in 30 minutes. Come up with an estimate of the number of skis sold in Australia annually.

framework: Estimate total Australian skiers by working from resort capacity and season length
Adjust for ski ownership life to convert total skiers to annual ski purchases
Note that hire vs. own distinction has minimal impact on the final estimate

questions.prompt: Estimate the number of skis sold in Australia per year.
questions.guidance: A strong answer structures the estimation in two steps: (1) size the total skier population, then (2) convert to annual ski purchases using an assumed product life. The candidate should state assumptions clearly and check whether the order of magnitude is reasonable.

math.setup: Step 1 – Total skiers per season: 5 major ski resort areas × 5,000 skier capacity each × 12-week season ÷ 1 week average stay = 300,000 skier-visits. Casebook rounds to ~250,000 skiers. Step 2 – Annual ski sales: assume each skier owns one pair of skis with a 5-year life, so 1/5 of skiers buy new skis each year.
steps: 5 resort areas × 5,000 capacity = 25,000 skiers at resorts at any one time
25,000 × 10 turnovers per season (12 weeks ÷ ~1 week/visit) = ~250,000 total skiers per season
250,000 skiers ÷ 5-year ski life = 50,000 skis sold per year
math.answer: Approximately 50,000 skis sold in Australia per year

recommendation: The Australian ski market is estimated at roughly 50,000 units per year
With a revolutionary new technology, the addressable market exists but is relatively small and seasonal
risks: Hire/rental equipment competes directly with ownership, potentially reducing the purchase market
Australia's ski season is short (~12 weeks), limiting repeat or impulse buying
Estimation relies on assumed resort capacity and visit length — actual figures could shift the result materially
next_steps: Validate resort capacity and average visit-length assumptions with industry data
Assess what share of skiers hire vs. own equipment to refine addressable market
Understand pricing and margin structure before committing to the distributor role
